# Danceify FAQ — Price, Coins, 17 Dance Styles, Dogs, Cats and Babies

URL: https://danceifyapp.com/faq.html
Updated: 2026-11-10

Answers about Danceify, the iPhone app that makes a person, baby, dog or cat dance from one photo: price, coins, the 17 styles, accounts and more.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Danceify - AI Dance Videos · iPhone and iPad app · facts current as of November 10, 2026

What is Danceify?

Danceify - AI Dance Videos is an iPhone and iPad app on the App Store (App Store ID 6760788471). It turns one photo of a person, a baby, a dog or a cat into a 10-second dance video, in any of 17 dance styles, and there are also Premium themed templates.

How does Danceify work?

Choose one of 17 dance styles or a Premium themed template, pick one photo of a person, a baby, a dog or a cat, and Danceify makes a dance video of about 10 seconds that you can save to your phone and share.

The process takes three steps:

- Pick a dance style from 17 options like EDM Shuffle, Salsa, Hip-hop, K-Pop or Ballet.
- Upload a photo from your camera roll — a person, dog, cat, or baby.
- Get your video: pick a track, tap CREATE and you get a dance video of about 10 seconds you can save to your phone and share.

What subjects can dance?

Danceify supports four subject types: adults (photo to dance video), babies (dancing baby video), dogs (make my dog dance video), and cats (AI cat dance). Each gets specialized AI choreography tuned to their body type and proportions. The AI handles the anatomy differences automatically — you just upload a photo.

How do pets dance?

Dogs and cats are rendered standing upright on their hind legs with species-specific choreography. The AI preserves your pet's breed, fur color, markings, and overall identity while applying natural-looking dance moves that match the selected style. The result looks like your actual pet busting moves — not a generic animal. See make my dog dance video and AI cat dance.

What dance styles are available?

Danceify offers 17 dance styles:

- EDM Shuffle — festival drop energy
- Salsa — Latin partner-style footwork and hip movement
- TikTok — Trending social media choreography
- Bollywood — Expressive Indian film-style dance
- Samba — High-energy Brazilian carnival moves
- Greek — Traditional Greek folk steps
- Hip-hop — Street-style grooves and isolations
- Ballet — Classical graceful movements
- Tango — Dramatic Argentine-style steps
- Flamenco — Passionate Spanish footwork
- Reggaeton — Latin urban rhythm and bounce
- Swing — Retro jazz-era swing moves
- Belly Dance — Fluid torso isolations and shimmies
- Hula — Hawaiian hand and hip storytelling
- Country Line — Western line dance steps
- K-Pop — Sharp Korean pop choreography
- Irish — Rapid footwork with upright posture

All 17 styles work with every subject type — adults, babies, dogs, and cats. There are also Premium themed templates.

Is Danceify free?

Danceify is free to download, with no account, sign-up or email; purchases go through your Apple Account. Videos use coins (◆): one-time coin packs start at $3.99 (US), and Creation Weekly is $11.99 a week in the US with 4,000 coins a week; eligible new subscribers may get the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins. A Regular video uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later (150 coins in earlier versions). The App Store shows the price for your country.

How much does Danceify cost?

Videos use coins (◆): one-time coin packs start at $3.99 (US), and Creation Weekly is $11.99 a week in the US with 4,000 coins a week; eligible new subscribers may get the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins. A Regular video uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later (150 coins in earlier versions). The App Store shows the price for your country.

Is there a free trial?

No, there is no free trial. From November 10, 2026, eligible new Creation Weekly subscribers get the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins, then $11.99 a week in the US, with your balance refilled up to 4,000 coins every week. The introductory offer is once per Apple Account, so if you have already had a free trial or an introductory offer, Creation Weekly starts at $11.99 a week. Cancel anytime in your iPhone's Settings, under Subscriptions. The App Store shows the price for your country before you confirm.

Can I cancel my subscription?

Yes, cancel anytime. On your iPhone, go to Settings → [Your Name] → Subscriptions → Danceify → Cancel Subscription, at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. When a paid plan ends, your coin balance stays and the weekly refills stop. On Creation Monthly and Creation Yearly, weekly refills continue for the rest of the period you paid for. No cancellation fees, no questions asked.

What happens to my photo?

Your photo is uploaded to our cloud storage and sent to the AI services that generate your video. We use it only for that, and we never sell it or use it for advertising. We delete it from our storage when your video is done, and in any case within hours. Our privacy policy names the services involved and says how long each kind of data is kept.

What kind of photo works best?

For the best results:

- Clear face visible — no sunglasses, masks, or heavy obstructions
- Good lighting — natural light or well-lit indoor shots
- Front-facing — the subject looking toward the camera
- One subject only — crop out other people or pets
- Reasonable resolution — avoid heavily compressed or blurry images

Avoid group photos, extreme angles, very dark images, or photos where the subject is far away in the frame.

Can I share the videos?

Absolutely. Save your dance video to your camera roll and share it anywhere you want — TikTok, Instagram Reels, Stories, iMessage, WhatsApp, email, or any other platform. Videos are rendered in a social-ready vertical format.

What if video generation fails?

If a generation fails, your coins are refunded automatically. If that does not happen, email us at danceify.app@gmail.com. Common reasons for failure include very low-quality photos, multiple subjects in one frame, or unusual poses. Try again with a different photo that has better lighting and a clearer view of the subject.

Is Danceify available on Android?

Danceify is an iPhone and iPad app on the App Store. You can download it from the Apple App Store. An Android version is not available at this time.

How do I find the right app on the App Store?

Its App Store name is Danceify - AI Dance Videos and its App Store ID is 6760788471: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6760788471. If an App Store page shows a different ID, it is a different app.

What language is the app in?

English, Japanese, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), Korean, German, French and Italian. The app follows your iPhone's language.

Can I use Danceify without a subscription?

Yes. One-time coin packs start at $3.99 (US); Creation Weekly is optional.

# Danceify — Support

URL: https://danceifyapp.com/support.html
Updated: 2026-11-08

Danceify support: how coins and subscriptions work, how to cancel or restore purchases, how long a video takes, and how to contact us.

## Support

Help · FAQ · Contact

We're here to help you get your groove on. Most questions are answered below — if you don't see yours, drop us a line.

### Frequently Asked

#### How do I get dances?

Every dance is fueled by coins. A Regular video uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later (150 coins in earlier versions). You can earn coins with a subscription (weekly, monthly, or yearly), or buy them one-time as a coin pack that never expires.

Weekly subscriptions: Starter ($4.99/wk, 1,200 coins), Creation ($11.99/wk, 4,000 coins), Advanced ($14.99/wk, 5,400 coins), Elite ($19.99/wk, 7,800 coins) or Prestige ($69.99/wk, 31,200 coins). Each week your balance is refilled up to the plan's coins; unused coins do not add up. There is no free trial. From November 10, 2026, eligible new Creation subscribers may get the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins, then $11.99 a week (one introductory offer per Apple Account). If you already subscribe to Creation Weekly at $9.99, you keep paying $9.99 a week and also get 4,000 coins a week.

Monthly & yearly subscriptions: Creation Monthly ($29.99/mo, 3,000 coins every week) or Creation Yearly ($149.99/yr, 1,200 coins every week). Each week of the period you paid for, your balance is topped up to the plan's weekly coins, even if you have turned auto-renew off; unused coins do not add up.

One-time coin packs: A $3.99 Starter Pack for first-time buyers (1,800 coins; the coin store stops showing it after you buy it), plus coin packs at $3.99 (1,400 coins), $9.99 (4,000), $21.99 (9,400), $45.99 (20,000) and $119.99 (53,000). None of them expire.

These are the United States prices in US dollars. Everywhere else the App and the App Store show the price in your own currency, as set by Apple for your country or region, before you buy.

Existing subscribers on Plus, Pro Weekly and Lite keep their plans without changes. Pro Monthly, Pro Yearly and Creator are no longer sold and do not renew; if you have one, it runs to the end of your current billing period.

#### How long does a video take to generate?

Videos in the 17 dance styles are usually ready in 2 to 5 minutes; Premium templates usually take 4 to 10 minutes. The app shows an estimate. In app version 5.28 and later, once your video has started you can leave the app: it is made on our servers, the finished video appears in your Library, and the app notifies you if notifications are on. In older versions, keep Danceify open until a video in the 17 dance styles is done.

#### Do purchased coins expire?

No. Coins you buy and coins from paid periods do not expire, unless Apple refunds that purchase. Subscription coins are refilled every week on every plan, including the monthly and yearly plans. If your plan started with a free trial (not offered to new subscribers from November 7, 2026), the coins that came with it are for the trial (1,200 or 3,000 coins, depending on your app version and the screen): if the app told you that unused trial coins expire, any you have not used expire when the trial ends, unless your paid subscription starts; otherwise they stay if you cancel. If your first payment is declined, unused trial coins are removed either way. Your first payment refills your balance up to your plan's weekly coins; a top-up adds nothing if your balance is already at or above that amount.

#### How do I cancel my subscription?

Open the Settings app on your iPhone, tap your name at the top, then Subscriptions. Find Danceify and tap Cancel. Subscriptions renew automatically unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. If you started a free trial before November 7, 2026: cancel at least 24 hours before it ends and you are not charged; your trial coins work until the trial ends. Unused coins from a 1,200-coin trial then expire; coins from a 3,000-coin trial stay. When a paid plan ends, your coin balance stays and the weekly refills stop. On Creation Monthly and Creation Yearly, weekly refills continue for the rest of the period you paid for.

#### How do I restore purchases?

In the app, go to Settings and tap "Restore Purchases". This restores an active subscription tied to your Apple Account. If coins you bought are missing afterwards, email us with the user ID shown in Settings.

#### Can I delete my data?

Yes. In the app, Settings → Delete Account removes your account, your coin history, your Premium dances and your Regular videos (app version 5.28 and later), with the videos and photos stored with them. It does not cancel a subscription; cancel that in your iPhone's Settings first. To delete everything else we hold, including anything stored under an earlier user ID and analytics data, or to ask for a copy of your data, email us at danceify.app@gmail.com with the user ID shown in the app's Settings page (or write from your account email if you signed in with one). The privacy policy has the details.

### Contact

For any other questions, bugs, or feedback: danceify.app@gmail.com

## AI Cat Dance

Danceify makes an AI cat dance video from one photo: your cat stands up on its hind legs and dances a 10-second routine in the style you choose, with music. It takes a few minutes in the iPhone app, with no sign-up. Dogs, babies and people dance too.

Download on theApp Store

The app's own CAT previews — Hula, Ballet, K-Pop and Flamenco

### How it works

01
Choose CAT and a style
Tap the CAT tab and pick one of 17 dance styles. The choreography is written for a cat's body, tail and whiskers, and each style has its own music.

02
Pick a photo of your cat
One cat, facing the camera, whole body visible, good light. The app first stands your cat up on its hind legs, then animates the dance.

03
Get the video
Pick a track and tap CREATE. The 10-second video renders on Danceify's servers in a few minutes and lands in your Library. Save it to your camera roll and share it anywhere.

### Questions people ask

#### Which app makes a cat dance from a photo?

Danceify - AI Dance Videos, an iPhone and iPad app on the App Store (App Store ID 6760788471). Pick one photo of your cat and one of 17 dance styles, and it makes a 10-second video of your cat dancing that you can save and share. It is free to download and needs no account; videos use coins.

#### Will it look like my cat?

The AI keeps the fur colour and pattern, face, ears, eyes and whiskers from your photo, and animates that cat on two legs in a photoreal style. A clear photo of the cat facing the camera, not curled up asleep, gives the most convincing result.

#### What photo of my cat works best?

One cat per photo, looking roughly at the camera, whole body visible, in even light. Avoid blurry shots, photos taken from above, and photos with several pets or people. A portrait (vertical) photo frames the dance best.

#### How long does an AI cat dance video take?

A few minutes. The video is made on Danceify's servers; the app shows an estimate while it renders (typically two to five minutes for the 17 dance styles, four to ten for Premium themed templates), and the finished video appears in your Library in the app. If a video fails to render, the coins it used are returned automatically.

#### Does Danceify work for dogs too?

Yes. There is a DOG tab with dog choreography for the same 17 styles; see make my dog dance video. Babies and people have their own modes as well.

#### Can my cat do a TikTok dance?

Yes. TikTok is one of the 17 dance styles: choose TikTok, pick a photo of your cat, and save the 10-second video to post.

#### Is it free, and do I need an account?

Danceify is free to download, with no account, sign-up or email; purchases go through your Apple Account. Videos use coins (◆): one-time coin packs start at $3.99 (US), and Creation Weekly is $11.99 a week in the US with 4,000 coins a week; eligible new subscribers may get the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins. A Regular video uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later (150 coins in earlier versions). The App Store shows the price for your country.

#### Can I share the cat video on TikTok or Instagram?

Yes. Each video is about 10 seconds long, comes with a music track, and saves to your camera roll, so you can post it to TikTok, Instagram Reels or Stories, or send it in iMessage or WhatsApp. A portrait photo gives the best social-ready framing.

### Questions people ask

#### What app turns a photo into a dance video?

Danceify - AI Dance Videos, an iPhone and iPad app on the App Store (App Store ID 6760788471). Pick one photo of a person, a baby, a dog or a cat and one of 17 dance styles, and it makes a 10-second dance video that you can save and share. It is free to download and needs no account; videos use coins.

#### How do I make a picture dance on iPhone?

Download Danceify from the App Store, choose a dance style, pick one photo of a person, a baby, a dog or a cat, and save the 10-second video.

#### What photo works best?

A standing, whole-body photo of one person facing the camera, in good light. Seated poses, close-ups, group shots and screenshots give poor or no dance. A portrait (vertical) photo frames the dance best.

#### Does it keep my face, or is it a face swap?

It keeps you. The AI animates the person in your photo with their own face, hair, skin tone and clothing locked in every frame; it does not paste your face onto another dancer. Results vary with the photo.

#### How long does it take?

A few minutes. The video is made on Danceify's servers; the app shows an estimate while it renders (typically two to five minutes for the 17 dance styles, four to ten for Premium themed templates), and the finished video appears in your Library in the app. If a video fails to render, the coins it used are returned automatically.

## Ballet AI Dance Video

Classical grace and elegance — AI-generated ballet choreography

Try Ballet →

### About Ballet

Ballet is the foundational discipline of Western theatrical dance, with roots stretching back to the Italian Renaissance courts of the fifteenth century. What began as elaborate court entertainments — performances staged for royalty featuring poetry, music, and movement — was formalized into a codified technique during the reign of France's Louis XIV. The Sun King established the Acad&eacute;mie Royale de Danse in 1661, creating the institutional framework that transformed ballet from courtly amusement into a professional art form with a standardized vocabulary that persists to this day.

Every ballet movement has a French name, and every student learns the same foundational positions. The five positions of the feet. The pli&eacute; — a controlled bend of the knees. The tendu — a sliding extension of the foot along the floor. The arabesque — balancing on one leg while the other extends behind the body. These building blocks combine into phrases of movement that prioritize line, turnout, and the illusion of effortlessness.

What makes ballet visually distinctive is its pursuit of vertical space. Dancers work against gravity: rising onto pointe (the tips of specially reinforced shoes), executing grand jet&eacute;s that seem to suspend them in midair, and holding extensions at heights that demand extraordinary flexibility and strength. The upper body — the &eacute;paulement — coordinates head, shoulders, and arms into positions that frame the movement and give it emotional direction.

Danceify's AI ballet mode captures the elongated lines, controlled port de bras (arm movements), and the smooth, continuous quality that distinguishes ballet from sharper dance forms. Generated videos show your subject moving with the lifted posture, pointed feet, and flowing transitions characteristic of classical technique. The AI emphasizes the grace and poise that make ballet one of the most visually striking dance forms ever developed, whether your subject is a person, a baby, or even a pet standing on its hind legs.

## Belly Dance AI Video

Mesmerizing isolations and fluid hip movement — AI-generated belly dance

Try Belly Dance →

### About Belly Dance

Belly dance — known in Arabic as raqs sharqi (literally "dance of the East") — is one of the oldest continuously practiced dance traditions in the world. Its origins trace to the fertility rituals and social celebrations of ancient Middle Eastern and North African cultures, with evidence of similar torso-articulated movement appearing in Egyptian tomb paintings dating back thousands of years. The dance evolved through centuries of cultural exchange across the Ottoman Empire, absorbing influences from Turkish, Persian, and Romani traditions.

The defining characteristic of belly dance is isolation — the ability to move one part of the body independently while the rest remains still. A belly dancer can circle their hips in a smooth figure-eight while their shoulders stay perfectly level, or ripple their abdominal muscles in a wave while their arms float in graceful arcs. This isolation technique requires extraordinary muscular control and body awareness that takes years to develop.

Key movements include the shimmy (a rapid vibration of the hips or shoulders), undulations (a rolling wave through the torso), hip drops and lifts (sharp accents created by alternately releasing and engaging the oblique muscles), and snake arms (a flowing wavelike motion through the arms and hands). The footwork is relatively simple — small steps, pivots, and turns — because the emphasis is on what happens above the waist.

Danceify's AI belly dance mode captures the hypnotic quality of this ancient art form. Generated videos showcase the signature hip movements, fluid torso undulations, and expressive arm work that make belly dance instantly recognizable. The AI produces movement that flows continuously, with the smooth, controlled quality that distinguishes trained belly dance from simple hip-shaking. Whether your subject is a person or a pet, the result is a mesmerizing sequence of isolations and shimmies set to an imaginary Middle Eastern rhythm.

## Bollywood AI Dance Video

Expressive theatrical energy — AI-generated Bollywood choreography

Try Bollywood →

### About Bollywood Dance

Bollywood dance is the vibrant, high-energy style that accompanies the song-and-dance sequences in Indian Hindi-language cinema. The term "Bollywood" itself is a portmanteau of Bombay (now Mumbai) and Hollywood, and the dance tradition it describes is equally hybrid — a kaleidoscopic fusion of classical Indian dance forms, folk traditions from across the subcontinent, and Western influences ranging from jazz to hip-hop to Latin movement.

The roots of Bollywood choreography lie in India's classical dance traditions: Bharatanatyam from Tamil Nadu, with its geometric precision and elaborate hand gestures (mudras); Kathak from North India, known for its intricate footwork and spinning turns (chakkars); and Odissi from Odisha, celebrated for its fluid tribhanga (three-bend) posture. Early Bollywood films drew heavily from these forms, but by the 1970s and 1980s, choreographers began incorporating disco, Western pop dance, and folk styles like bhangra (the energetic harvest dance of Punjab) and garba (the circular stick dance of Gujarat).

What makes Bollywood dance unique is its theatrical expressiveness. Every movement tells a story. Abhinaya — the art of expression — is paramount. Eyebrows lift, hands gesture meaningfully, the entire body becomes a vehicle for emotion. A Bollywood routine might transition from coy flirtation to triumphant celebration to dramatic heartbreak within a single song, each shift conveyed through movement as much as through lyrics.

Danceify's AI Bollywood mode captures the exuberant, larger-than-life energy that defines this style. Generated videos feature sweeping arm movements, expressive hand gestures, rhythmic shoulder shimmies, and the joyful, celebratory quality that makes Bollywood choreography beloved worldwide. The AI delivers movement that feels like a wedding scene or a festival sequence — colorful, energetic, and emotionally charged, whether your subject is a person dancing at a sangeet or a pet performing on its hind legs.

## Country Line Dance AI Video

Honky-tonk swagger — AI-generated country line dance moves

Try Country →

### About Country Line Dance

Country line dancing is one of America's most popular social dance forms, a tradition where rows of dancers perform the same choreographed steps in unison without needing a partner. Its roots intertwine several threads of American dance history: the contra dances and reels brought by English and Scottish settlers, the square dance calls that evolved on the frontier, and the two-step and waltz patterns that became staples of Texas honky-tonks in the mid-twentieth century.

The modern line dance explosion began in the early 1990s when Billy Ray Cyrus released "Achy Breaky Heart" and a simple line dance routine spread through country bars nationwide virtually overnight. But the form had been building for decades before that. The Electric Slide (1976), the Tush Push (1980s), and the Boot Scootin' Boogie (1992) established the template: a repeating sequence of steps performed in lines, typically 32 or 64 counts, with a quarter-turn at certain points so dancers face all four walls during the course of the dance.

Line dance vocabulary draws from country-western partner dance fundamentals. Grapevines — side-step, cross-behind, side-step — are ubiquitous. Heel touches, toe taps, and kick-ball-changes add rhythmic punctuation. Pivots and quarter-turns change the dancer's facing direction. The upper body stays relaxed and natural — no elaborate arm choreography — with thumbs sometimes hooked in belt loops or hands held loosely at the sides. The vibe is communal, accessible, and fun: line dancing is designed so anyone can join the floor after watching for a few bars.

Danceify's AI country line dance mode captures the boot-stomping, laid-back energy of a Friday night at the dance hall. Generated videos show your subject performing with the clean, synchronized footwork and easygoing confidence that define the style. The AI delivers movement with country dance's characteristic swagger — heel strikes, hip shifts, smooth turns, and the unpretentious groove of someone who's been dancing to country radio since they could walk.

### About EDM Shuffle

EDM Shuffle is a fast footwork dance done to electronic dance music. The feet carry the dance with quick heel-and-toe steps, slides and kicks that land on the beat, while the arms and upper body stay loose.

Most routines are built from a small set of steps. In the running man, one knee lifts while the standing foot slides back, then the feet switch. In the T-step, the standing foot swivels in and out while the other foot kicks out to the side. Dancers string these steps together and add spins and kicks to fit the music.

## Flamenco AI Dance Video

Fierce Spanish footwork and drama — AI-generated flamenco

Try Flamenco →

### About Flamenco

Flamenco is the soul of Andalusia, born in the southern Spanish region where Romani, Moorish, Jewish, and Castilian cultures collided over centuries. UNESCO recognized it as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010, but its origins are far older and more contested than any official designation suggests. The art form crystallized in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries in cities like Seville, Jerez de la Frontera, and C&aacute;diz, emerging from the marginalized Romani communities who used music and dance as vehicles for expressing grief, defiance, joy, and longing.

Flamenco is built on three pillars: cante (song), toque (guitar), and baile (dance). The dance cannot be understood without the other two — the dancer responds to the singer's emotional arc and the guitarist's rhythmic patterns in real time. The concept of duende — an untranslatable term describing a state of raw, transcendent emotion that overtakes the performer — is flamenco's highest aspiration. When duende arrives, the dancer stops performing and starts channeling.

The footwork, called zapateado, is flamenco's percussion section. Dancers wear hard-soled shoes and use the ball, heel, and flat of the foot to create intricate rhythmic patterns at extraordinary speed — a skilled bailaora can produce sounds faster than a snare drummer. Above the waist, the braceo (arm work) and floreo (hand flourishes) create sweeping, serpentine lines through space, with wrists rotating and fingers trailing in spiraling patterns. The torso remains tall and proud, the chin slightly lifted, projecting an attitude of fierce dignity.

Danceify's AI flamenco mode captures the fire and precision of this deeply emotional art form. Generated videos feature the sharp footwork accents, the dramatic arm extensions, and the proud upright carriage that define flamenco movement. The AI delivers the contrast that makes flamenco visually arresting: explosive bursts of zapateado followed by suspended pauses, rapid turns resolving into statuesque poses, and the overall intensity of a dancer who commands every inch of their stage with absolute authority.

# Greek Dance AI Video Generator — Danceify

## Greek Dance AI Video

Traditional folk movement and syrtaki spirit — AI-generated Greek dance

Try Greek Dance →

### About Greek Dance

Greek dance is among the oldest documented dance traditions in Western civilization, with depictions appearing on pottery, frescoes, and sculptures dating to the Minoan and Mycenaean civilizations over three thousand years ago. The ancient Greeks considered dance (choreia) essential to education, worship, and civic life — Plato himself argued that dance training was vital to a well-rounded citizen. This deep cultural reverence for movement has carried forward through millennia, making Greek folk dance one of the most continuously practiced traditions on Earth.

The most internationally recognized Greek dance is the syrtaki — popularized by Anthony Quinn in the 1964 film "Zorba the Greek" — but it's actually a modern choreographic creation by composer Mikis Theodorakis, blending elements of two authentic folk dances. The hasapiko (butchers' dance) is a slow, dignified line dance originating from the butchers' guild of Constantinople, with measured side-steps and precise leg lifts. The hasaposerviko is its faster cousin, building to a euphoric tempo where dancers leap and kick with abandon.

Authentic Greek folk dance is extraordinarily diverse — each region has its own styles. The kalamatianos from the Peloponnese is a twelve-step circle dance in 7/8 time, with a leader who improvises flourishes while the line follows a basic pattern. The tsamiko is a heroic men's dance from the mountains, with dramatic leaps and slow, deliberate movements. The pentozali from Crete is famously fast and athletic, with high kicks and rapid footwork. What unites all Greek dances is the circle or line formation, where dancers connect by holding hands, shoulders, or a shared handkerchief, creating a physical chain of community.

Danceify's AI Greek dance mode captures the communal joy and rhythmic footwork that characterize this ancient tradition. Generated videos show your subject moving with the measured steps, kicks, and arm-extended posture of a dancer in a Greek taverna celebration — starting slow and building in intensity, with the proud carriage and grounded footwork that make Greek dance feel like a physical expression of kefi, the Greek concept of passionate, uninhibited joy.

## Hip-Hop AI Dance Video

Try Hip-Hop →

### About Hip-Hop Dance

Hip-hop dance emerged from the streets of New York City in the early 1970s, born alongside the broader hip-hop culture that included DJing, MCing, and graffiti. What began as informal movement at block parties in the Bronx evolved into one of the most influential dance forms of the modern era. Breaking (also called b-boying) was among the first distinct styles, with dancers performing athletic floor work, freezes, and power moves to the rhythmic breaks in funk and soul records.

Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, hip-hop dance branched into multiple sub-styles. Popping uses rapid muscle contractions to create a snapping visual effect. Locking combines fluid movement with sudden pauses and exaggerated gestures. Krumping, emerging from South Los Angeles in the early 2000s, channels raw emotion through aggressive chest pops, arm swings, and stomps. Each sub-style carries its own vocabulary, history, and community.

What makes hip-hop unique among dance styles is its improvisational core. Cyphers — circles where dancers take turns freestyling — remain central to the culture. The emphasis is on individual expression, musicality, and swagger rather than rigid technique. A hip-hop dancer's style is a personal signature.

Danceify's AI captures the sharp isolations, rhythmic bounce, and attitude that define hip-hop movement. When you generate a hip-hop dance video, you'll see crisp body rolls, head nods synced to the beat, and the grounded stance that distinguishes street dance from other forms. The AI understands the difference between the smooth glide of a pop-and-lock sequence and the explosive energy of a breaking power move, delivering authentic-looking choreography that respects the style's roots.

## Hula AI Dance Video

Hawaiian storytelling through movement — AI-generated hula dance

Try Hula →

### About Hula

Hula is far more than a dance — it is the living archive of Hawaiian culture, a tradition through which history, mythology, genealogy, and spiritual beliefs have been preserved and transmitted across generations in a culture that had no written language until the nineteenth century. Every hula tells a story. The hand gestures represent specific words and concepts — rain, ocean, love, mountain, wind — while the footwork and hip movement provide the rhythmic foundation that carries the narrative forward.

Two major forms exist. Hula kahiko (ancient hula) is the older tradition, performed to chanting (oli) and percussion instruments like the ipu (gourd drum), the p&umacr;niu (coconut shell drum), and the &lsquo;ili&lsquo;ili (river stones used as castanets). Kahiko is powerful and grounded, with strong stamps, deep knee bends, and an intensity that connects the dancer to the earth and to ancestral spirits. Hula &lsquo;auana (modern hula) emerged in the nineteenth century after Christian missionaries suppressed the practice. When King David Kal&amacr;kaua revived hula in the 1880s, it absorbed Western musical influences — ukulele, slack-key guitar, steel guitar — and developed a softer, more flowing style.

The foundation of all hula is the vamp — a basic stepping pattern performed with bent knees that keeps the dancer low to the ground. The hips sway naturally as a consequence of the weight shifts, not as a separate embellishment. Above the waist, the hands and arms create the hula hands — flowing, precise gestures that illustrate the mele (song or chant). A hand waving from side to side might represent ocean waves; fingers fluttering downward might signify rain; arms extended outward could indicate a mountain range.

Danceify's AI hula mode captures the graceful, narrative quality that distinguishes hula from purely rhythmic dance forms. Generated videos show your subject moving with the flowing arm gestures, gentle hip sway, and grounded footwork that characterize hula's storytelling tradition. The AI produces movement with the serene, connected quality of a dancer performing at a lu&lsquo;au beneath palm trees — unhurried, expressive, and deeply rooted in the rhythms of the Hawaiian islands.

## Irish Step Dance AI Video

Disciplined footwork and Celtic precision — AI-generated Irish dance

Try Irish Dance →

### About Irish Step Dance

Irish step dance is one of the most visually distinctive dance forms in the world, instantly recognizable by its defining paradox: extraordinary speed and complexity below the waist paired with an almost completely still upper body. Arms held rigid at the sides, back ramrod straight, chin level — while below, the feet execute intricate patterns of clicks, stamps, hops, and aerial movements at speeds that can exceed ten beats per second.

The origins of Irish step dance are debated, but most historians trace its development to the eighteenth-century dancing masters who traveled between towns in rural Ireland, teaching steps and creating new dances for local communities. These itinerant teachers competed with each other for students, driving innovation in footwork complexity. The rigid upper body is often attributed to the cramped spaces where lessons took place — kitchen tables, barn doors, sometimes literally dancing on a door laid flat — but it likely also reflects the formal deportment expectations of the era.

Two shoe types create two fundamentally different sounds and styles. Soft shoes (ghillies for women, reel shoes for men) produce a whisper-quiet dance where the emphasis is on elevation, pointed toes, and the visual beauty of crossing and uncrossing the feet. Hard shoes (heavy shoes with fiberglass tips and heels) transform the dancer into a percussionist, producing thunderous rhythmic patterns called trebles — rapid-fire beats created by striking the toe and heel in alternation. The hard shoe treble is to Irish dance what the zapateado is to flamenco: the style's rhythmic signature.

Danceify's AI Irish dance mode captures the vertical precision and rapid footwork that define this Celtic tradition. Generated videos show your subject with the characteristic erect posture and still arms while the feet perform quick, clean step patterns beneath. The AI delivers the contrast that makes Irish dance so striking: absolute stillness above the waist and explosive rhythmic movement below it, whether your subject is performing a light shoe reel or a thundering hard shoe treble.

### About K-Pop Dance

K-Pop dance is the choreographic engine of South Korea's global pop culture phenomenon. Unlike most Western pop where dance is secondary to vocals, K-Pop treats choreography as an equal pillar of the performance. Every comeback — the industry term for a new single release — arrives with a meticulously crafted dance routine designed to be visually stunning on stage, in music videos, and on social media. The choreography is typically created by specialized dance crews like Kiel Tutin, Rie Hata, or the choreographers at 1MILLION Dance Studio.

What defines K-Pop dance is its precision. Groups like BTS, BLACKPINK, SEVENTEEN, and aespa perform with razor-sharp synchronization — every angle, every extension, every head turn matched across all members. The choreography blends hip-hop foundations with contemporary dance, jazz, and even martial arts-inspired movements. Point choreography — the signature move designed to be instantly recognizable and endlessly imitable — is a deliberate strategy, creating viral moments that fans replicate in dance challenges worldwide.

Formation changes are another hallmark. K-Pop groups constantly shift positions, creating kaleidoscopic patterns when viewed from above. The transitions between formations are as choreographed as the moves themselves, with members weaving through each other in rehearsed sequences that look effortless but require hundreds of hours of practice.

Danceify's K-Pop style captures the clean lines, sharp isolations, and polished energy of idol choreography. The AI generates movement that emphasizes precise arm angles, controlled body waves, and the confident facial expressions that K-Pop fans call "stage presence." Your generated video will have that unmistakable K-Pop look: tight, rehearsed, and camera-ready, as if your subject just debuted with a top-tier entertainment agency.

# Reggaeton AI Dance Video Generator — Danceify

## Reggaeton AI Dance Video

Latin urban heat and dembow rhythm — AI-generated reggaeton moves

Try Reggaeton →

### About Reggaeton Dance

Reggaeton emerged in the housing projects of Puerto Rico during the early 1990s, a musical and cultural movement born from the collision of Jamaican dancehall, Latin American hip-hop, and Caribbean electronic music. The genre's rhythmic foundation is the dembow riddim — a syncopated beat pattern originally sampled from Shabba Ranks' 1990 dancehall track "Dem Bow" — which provides the unmistakable boom-ch-boom-chick that drives nearly every reggaeton song ever made.

The dance that evolved alongside this music is visceral and body-driven. Perreo, the most iconic reggaeton dance style, emphasizes hip movement, low stances, and rhythmic body rolls synchronized to the dembow beat. Unlike formal partner dances with prescribed steps, perreo is improvisational and responsive — dancers react to the music's energy shifts, dropping low during bass-heavy drops and riding the rhythm with undulating torso movements during melodic passages.

As reggaeton conquered global charts through artists like Daddy Yankee, Bad Bunny, J Balvin, and Karol G, its dance vocabulary expanded. Modern reggaeton choreography incorporates elements from hip-hop isolations, Afro-Caribbean body waves, and even TikTok-era viral moves. The style has become a lingua franca of Latin nightlife worldwide — from San Juan to Medell&iacute;n to Madrid to Miami, the dembow beat hits and everyone knows how to move.

Danceify's AI reggaeton engine delivers the grounded, hip-driven energy that defines the style. Generated videos show your subject moving with the low center of gravity, rhythmic hip isolations, and confident swagger that reggaeton demands. The AI captures the bounce — that irresistible response to the dembow pattern where the body dips and rises in sync with the beat's kick and snare. The result feels like a Saturday night at a Latin club, bottled into a ten-second AI video.

### How To Create a Reggaeton Dance Video

01

Download Danceify
Get Danceify free from the App Store. Available on iPhone and iPad.

## Salsa AI Dance Video

Latin fire and Cuban motion — AI-generated salsa choreography

Try Salsa →

### About Salsa Dance

Salsa was forged in the dance halls of 1960s and 1970s New York City, where Cuban son, mambo, and Puerto Rican bomba collided with jazz and funk in the barrios of Spanish Harlem and the Bronx. The term "salsa" — literally "sauce" — was popularized by Fania Records and its roster of musicians who blended these traditions into something urgent and new. The dance that emerged alongside the music borrowed the structured partner framework of Cuban casino rueda while adding the linear footwork and flashy turn patterns favored by New York dancers.

At its core, salsa is danced on a quick-quick-slow rhythm pattern timed to the clave, the five-stroke rhythmic backbone of Afro-Cuban music. Dancers shift their weight across three beats, pause on the fourth, and repeat. This produces the rolling hip motion called Cuban motion — not a deliberate hip shake, but the natural consequence of proper weight transfer through bent and straightened knees. The upper body stays relatively still while the lower body does the talking.

Two dominant lineages exist today. LA-style salsa (salsa on 1) favors dramatic dips, aerials, and showy performance. New York-style (salsa on 2) emphasizes smooth musicality and connection, breaking on the second beat for a more grounded, jazz-influenced feel. Both share the same foundational steps but differ in timing, attitude, and emphasis.

Danceify's AI salsa engine captures the essence of Latin partner-style movement: the quick cross-body leads, the spinning turn sequences, and the rhythmic hip sway that makes salsa instantly recognizable. When you generate a salsa video, your subject moves with the warm, confident energy of a Saturday-night social dance floor — weight low, shoulders relaxed, feet tracing clean patterns beneath fluid upper-body styling.

## Samba AI Dance Video

Brazilian carnival energy — AI-generated samba with quick footwork

Try Samba →

### About Samba Dance

Samba is the rhythmic heartbeat of Brazil, a dance tradition so central to national identity that it's virtually inseparable from the country itself. Its origins lie in the Afro-Brazilian communities of Bahia in northeastern Brazil, where West African rhythmic traditions brought by enslaved people merged with indigenous Brazilian and Portuguese colonial influences. The word "samba" likely derives from the Kimbundu term "semba," referring to a type of ritual dance involving a belly bump — an invitation to dance that became the seed of an entire cultural movement.

The samba no p&eacute; — samba "in the foot" — is the foundational solo style most people picture when they think of samba. It's characterized by a rapid alternating bounce step where the dancer shifts weight from foot to foot in a quick three-step pattern (1-a-2), with the knees softly bending and the hips naturally swaying as a result. The footwork is fast — often 100 beats per minute or more — but the upper body remains surprisingly relaxed, with arms open and free.

During Carnaval, Brazil's annual pre-Lenten celebration, samba reaches its most spectacular expression. Passistas (featured samba dancers) perform in elaborate costumes with breathtaking speed, their feet moving so fast they seem to blur while their torsos remain steady and their faces radiate pure joy. Each samba school — the community organizations that compete in Carnaval — develops its own choreographic identity, with hundreds of dancers moving in coordinated formations through the Samb&oacute;dromo.

Danceify's AI samba mode captures the infectious energy and lightning-fast footwork that make samba one of the world's most exciting dance forms. Generated videos show your subject bouncing with the characteristic samba spring — that elastic quality where the body seems to perpetually rise and fall — accompanied by hip sway, open arm styling, and the irrepressible sense of celebration that samba carries in every step. The AI delivers movement that feels like Carnaval compressed into ten seconds.

## Swing AI Dance Video

Vintage Lindy Hop joy — AI-generated swing dance moves

Try Swing →

### About Swing Dance

Swing dance was born in Harlem during the late 1920s and early 1930s, a direct physical response to the swinging jazz music that was revolutionizing American popular culture. The Lindy Hop — named, according to legend, after Charles Lindbergh's transatlantic "hop" — emerged at the Savoy Ballroom, a racially integrated dance hall on Lenox Avenue where some of the era's most innovative social dancers tested new moves against the music of bands led by Chick Webb, Count Basie, and Benny Goodman.

What made swing revolutionary was its breakaway — a moment where partners separated from closed position into open position, creating space for individual improvisation. This simple structural innovation opened a universe of possibilities. Dancers could swing out, add solo jazz steps, attempt aerial moves, and reconnect, all within the elastic framework of the basic swing rhythm. The dance breathed with the music, stretching and compressing in response to the band's dynamics.

Swing encompasses several related styles. Lindy Hop is the original, characterized by its eight-count basic, athletic aerials, and deep connection to jazz music. East Coast Swing simplified Lindy into a six-count pattern more accessible to casual social dancers. West Coast Swing evolved on the West Coast with a slotted, smoother style suited to blues and R&B. Jive sped things up into a high-energy competition form. All share the same DNA: a bouncy, grounded connection to the music's swing feel.

Danceify's AI swing mode captures the irrepressible joy and rhythmic bounce that define this dance family. Generated videos feature the elastic, bouncy quality of swing movement — the triple steps, the rock steps, and the swinging momentum that makes the style feel like pure musical happiness translated into physical form. The AI delivers movement with the grounded, connected quality of a Savoy Ballroom regular: relaxed shoulders, active feet, and an infectious grin's worth of energy in every step.

## Tango AI Dance Video

Dramatic intensity and passion — AI-generated Argentine tango

Try Tango →

### About Tango

The tango was born in the working-class neighborhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo during the late nineteenth century, a product of the cultural collision between European immigrants, African descendants, and criollo (native-born) populations in the R&iacute;o de la Plata region. Italian, Spanish, and Eastern European immigrants crowded into conventillos (tenement houses) alongside Afro-Argentine communities, and in the patios and bars of neighborhoods like La Boca and San Telmo, their musical and movement traditions fused into something entirely new.

The earliest tangos drew from the milonga (a faster, more rhythmic predecessor), the habanera (a Cuban rhythm that arrived via sailors), and African candombe drumming traditions. The dance that emerged was originally improvised, intimate, and slightly scandalous — partners held each other in a close embrace that shocked polite society. By the 1910s, tango had traveled to Paris, where it became a sensation in ballrooms and caf&eacute;s, and from there it conquered the world.

What distinguishes tango from other partner dances is its improvisational conversation. There are no predetermined step patterns. The leader communicates direction through subtle shifts in the embrace — a slight rotation of the torso, a gentle press of the hand — and the follower responds in real time. This creates a dance that feels like a wordless dialogue: question and answer, tension and release, advance and retreat. The ocho (a figure-eight pivot), the gancho (a hooking leg movement), and the volcada (a dramatic lean) are vocabulary, not choreography — tools for expression rather than fixed routines.

Danceify's AI tango mode captures the dramatic, floor-bound intensity that makes tango one of the most emotionally charged dance forms in the world. Generated videos feature the controlled walks, sharp direction changes, and tension-filled pauses that define the style. The AI delivers movement with tango's characteristic groundedness — feet sliding close to the floor, weight always committed, the body moving as a single connected unit with deliberate, smoldering intent.

Try TikTok Viral →

### About TikTok Dance Culture

TikTok has fundamentally reshaped how dance moves spread through culture. Before TikTok, a new dance might take months or years to travel from its origin community to mainstream awareness. Now, a choreographic idea conceived in a bedroom in Lagos or Manila can reach a billion screens within 48 hours. The platform's short-form video format — typically 15 to 60 seconds — has created a new category of choreography: moves designed specifically to be learned quickly, performed in tight spaces, and read clearly on a phone screen held in portrait orientation.

TikTok dances share several structural traits. They tend to use the upper body and arms heavily, since most creators film from the waist up. The choreography is deliberately learnable — usually four to eight distinct moves strung together in a repeating pattern that matches the hook of a song. Complexity is traded for catchiness. The Renegade, the Savage, the Say So, the Corvette Corvette — each became a global phenomenon not because they were technically difficult, but because they were satisfying to perform and instantly recognizable.

The cultural engine behind TikTok dance is the challenge — a social prompt where users recreate a specific routine and post their version. This mechanic turns passive viewers into active participants. It also means that TikTok choreography must work across all body types, skill levels, and environments. The best TikTok dances look good whether performed by a trained dancer in a studio or a teenager in a kitchen.

Danceify's TikTok Viral style captures the punchy, camera-friendly energy that defines platform-native choreography. Generated videos feature the kind of moves that feel instantly shareable: crisp arm patterns, rhythmic body rolls, and attitude-driven gestures timed to imaginary beat drops. The AI produces movement optimized for the vertical frame — expressive upper-body work, clean transitions, and the confident, direct-to-camera energy that drives engagement. Your generated video arrives ready to post.

### How do I make it?

#### 01 Download Danceify

Get Danceify - AI Dance Videos from the App Store. Free to download; no account, sign-up or email.

#### 02 Choose who is dancing

On Home, tap ADULT, BABY, DOG or CAT. One subject per video.

#### 03 Pick a style and a photo

Choose a dance style from the table above. Then pick one photo from your camera roll: one person or pet, whole body visible, good light, facing the camera. Pick a track in the MUSIC row.

#### 04 Tap CREATE, then save and send

Danceify makes a 10-second video. You can change the track on the player. Save it to your camera roll and send it by Messages, WhatsApp or email, or post it to Instagram or TikTok.

### Can the dog, the cat or the baby dance?

Yes, and these are the videos families send most. Use the DOG, CAT or BABY tab, and one photo where the whole body is visible. A dog or cat can be sitting or standing in the photo; the app stands them up for the dance and keeps their markings. For a baby, a clear face and a simple background help. Costumes and props in the photo can confuse the app about body shape, so a plain photo of the pet usually works better than one in a full outfit; a hat is fine.

For more detail, see dog dance video tips, AI cat dance and baby dance video tips.

### Can I put the whole family in one video?

Not in one video. The app expects one subject per photo; crop a group photo down to one person before you pick it. A family of four is four videos, each 250 coins. You can send them one after another in the group chat, or combine them in your phone's video editor if you want a single clip.

### How long does it take?

A few minutes per video, from choosing the photo to a saved clip. You do not need to prepare anything in advance; you can make the video on December 24 and send it the same evening.

### What does it cost?

Danceify is free to download, with no account. Videos use coins (◆): one-time coin packs start at $3.99 (US), and Creation Weekly is $11.99 a week in the US with 4,000 coins a week; eligible new subscribers may get the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins. There is no free trial. A Regular video uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later (150 coins in earlier versions), so 1,200 coins is 4 videos and 4,000 coins is 16. The App Store shows the price for your country. Full details: Danceify pricing explained.

### What happens to the family photo?

Danceify's privacy policy says this about photos: "We keep an uploaded photo only while your video is being made. It is deleted from our storage when the video is finished, fails or is cancelled — normally within minutes — and a clean-up that runs every hour deletes any photo older than six hours." It also says: "We do not use your photos or videos to train AI models." The photo is sent to the AI services that generate the video; the privacy policy names them and how long they keep files.

Two rules from the same policy apply to holiday photos in particular: "Only upload a photo of another person if they have agreed, and a photo of a child only if you are the child's parent or legal guardian."

Download Danceify on the App Store

Facts current as of November 10, 2026. Danceify is available on iOS. Creation Weekly: $11.99/week (US), no free trial; eligible new subscribers may get the first week for $2.99. Cancel anytime.

No. As of November 10, 2026, the 17 dance styles are what there is: EDM Shuffle, Salsa, TikTok, Bollywood, Samba, Greek, Hip-hop, Ballet, Tango, Flamenco, Reggaeton, Swing, Belly Dance, Hula, Country Line, K-Pop and Irish, plus Premium themed templates. None is a holiday template.

Which dance style works for a Christmas card video?

Swing, Ballet, Irish and Country Line suit a festive card. For New Year's Eve, EDM Shuffle, Salsa or TikTok fit a party clip. Any of the 17 styles works; the holiday feel comes from the photo, for example a sweater, a tree or a hat.

Can my dog, cat or baby be in the holiday dance video?

Yes. Tap DOG, CAT or BABY on Home and use one photo with the whole body visible. One subject per video; a family of four is four videos.

# Danceify Pricing Explained (November 2026): Is It Free, the $2.99 First Week, What Coins Buy

URL: https://danceifyapp.com/blog/danceify-pricing-explained.html
Updated: 2026-11-10

Danceify is free to download; videos use coins. Coin packs from $3.99 (US), Creation Weekly $11.99 a week with 4,000 coins, first week $2.99 for eligible new subscribers, no free trial. Local prices, how to cancel.

## Danceify Pricing Explained (November 2026)

Prices and coins · Published November 10, 2026 · Updated November 10, 2026 · 6 min read

Short answer
Danceify - AI Dance Videos, an iPhone and iPad app, is free to download, and making a video uses coins. As of November 10, 2026, one-time coin packs start at $3.99 (US), and the Creation Weekly subscription is $11.99 a week in the US with 4,000 coins a week. There is no free trial; eligible new subscribers get the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins, then $11.99 a week.

Key facts

- App: Danceify - AI Dance Videos, App Store ID 6760788471. iPhone and iPad only.
- Download: free. No account, sign-up or email; purchases go through your Apple Account.
- Coins (◆): a Regular video uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later (150 in earlier versions). Premium videos cost more.
- Coin packs: one-time, from $3.99 (US).
- Creation Weekly: $11.99 a week (US), 4,000 coins a week.
- Free trial: none since November 7, 2026.
- Introductory offer: from November 10, 2026, the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins, then $11.99 a week. One per Apple Account.
- Earlier subscribers: people who subscribed at $9.99 keep $9.99, with 4,000 coins a week.

This article explains every price in Danceify as of November 10, 2026, in plain terms: what is free, what coins are, what the $2.99 first week is, what the App Store shows in other countries, and how to cancel. If anything here disagrees with what the App Store shows you, the App Store is right: it shows the price for your country and the terms before you confirm.

Download Danceify Free

### Is Danceify free?

The download is free. You can install Danceify from the App Store, open it, browse the 17 dance styles and the preview videos, and pick a photo without paying anything. There is no account to create and no email to give; purchases go through your Apple Account.

Making a video is not free. Each video uses coins (◆), and you get coins by buying a one-time coin pack or by subscribing to Creation Weekly. There is no free video and no free trial. If you read somewhere that Danceify has a free trial, that was true before November 7, 2026; it is not true now.

### What are coins, and how many does a video use?

Coins are the in-app currency. The app shows your balance, and each video takes coins from it.

- A Regular video, one of the 17 dance styles (EDM Shuffle, Salsa, TikTok, Bollywood, Samba, Greek, Hip-hop, Ballet, Tango, Flamenco, Reggaeton, Swing, Belly Dance, Hula, Country Line, K-Pop, Irish), uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later. In earlier versions it uses 150 coins.
- A Premium video, one of the themed templates, costs more coins. The app shows the cost before you create it.

Coins you buy and coins from paid subscription periods do not expire, unless Apple refunds that purchase. When a paid plan ends, your coin balance stays and the weekly refills stop. See Support for the full rules.

### How much do coin packs cost?

One-time coin packs start at $3.99 (US). A coin pack is not a subscription: you pay once, the coins are added to your balance, and nothing renews. This is the option to choose if you want to make a few videos and stop.

The App Store shows the price for your country. We do not list the local prices of coin packs here, because they vary by country; open the app and the App Store shows your price before you buy.

If you specifically want to avoid a subscription, see AI dance video app without a subscription.

### What is Creation Weekly?

Creation Weekly is Danceify's subscription. In the US it costs $11.99 a week and gives 4,000 coins a week. At 250 coins per Regular video, 4,000 coins cover 16 Regular videos a week. It renews automatically every week until you cancel.

People who subscribed earlier at $9.99 a week are not moved to the new price: they keep $9.99 and also get 4,000 coins a week.

### What is the $2.99 first week?

From November 10, 2026, eligible new Creation Weekly subscribers get the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins. After that first week the subscription continues at $11.99 a week with 4,000 coins a week, unless you cancel before the week ends.

Three details matter:

- It is an introductory offer, not a free trial. You pay $2.99 on day one.
- You get one introductory offer per Apple Account. If your Apple Account has already used one, the App Store will not show it again.
- The App Store shows the terms and the local price before you confirm, so you can see exactly what you will pay and when.

1,200 coins is enough for 4 Regular videos at 250 coins each, with 200 coins left over that stay on your balance.

### What does Danceify cost in my country?

The App Store sets the price in your local currency. These are the Creation Weekly prices in App Store Connect as of November 10, 2026: the introductory first week, then the weekly price.

Country | First week (eligible new subscribers) | Then per week

United States | $2.99 | $11.99

United Kingdom | £2.99 | £11.99

Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Portugal | €2.99 | €11.99

Mexico | MX$69 | MX$239

Brazil | R$19,90 | R$71,90

Japan | ¥500 | ¥1,800

Korea | ₩4,400 | ₩16,800

Coin packs: from $3.99 (US); the App Store shows the price for your country. Local prices can change; the App Store is always the current source.

### Which option should I pick?

There is no wrong answer; it depends on how many videos you want.

- One or two videos, no commitment: a one-time coin pack from $3.99 (US).
- A few videos this week, and you are eligible for the offer: Creation Weekly at $2.99 for the first week, with 1,200 coins (4 Regular videos). Cancel before the week ends if you do not want $11.99 a week after that.
- Many videos every week: Creation Weekly at $11.99 a week, with 4,000 coins (16 Regular videos) a week.

### How do I cancel Creation Weekly?

Subscriptions are managed by Apple, not inside the app. Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad, tap your name at the top (your Apple Account), then Subscriptions. Find Danceify and tap Cancel. Subscriptions renew automatically unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Deleting the app does not cancel a subscription.

After you cancel, your coin balance stays and the weekly refills stop. To restore an active subscription on a new phone, open the app, go to Settings and tap "Restore Purchases". Refunds are handled by Apple; see Support for the steps.

### What you get for the money

Every video is a 10-second dance video made from one photo of a person, a baby, a dog or a cat, in one of the 17 dance styles. You pick a track in the app, and you can change it on the player after the video is made. Videos save to your phone and can be shared to TikTok, Instagram, Messages or anywhere else. For the steps, see How to make an AI dance video; for what a photo should look like, see photo to dance video.

Platforms · Published November 10, 2026 · Updated November 10, 2026 · 4 min read

Short answer

Key facts

- Name on the App Store: Danceify - AI Dance Videos. App Store ID 6760788471.

- Not on: Android, Google Play, the web, Mac or Windows.

People ask this question in several forms: "Danceify APK", "Danceify for Android", "Danceify Google Play", "Danceify online". The answer to all of them is the same. The app exists for iPhone and iPad and nowhere else. This page explains what that means in practice and what you can do if you or the person you want to share with has an Android phone.

### Why is there no Android version?

Danceify is built for iOS. It is sold through the Apple App Store, and purchases, subscriptions and refunds go through your Apple Account. There is no Google Play listing, no APK to download, and no plan we can announce for one. If that changes, this page will say so; the date at the top tells you when it was last checked.

Any file called a "Danceify APK" on a download site is not from us. We do not publish an Android app, so we cannot say what such a file contains. Do not install it.

### Is there a web version I can use on any device?

No. Danceify does not make videos in a browser. This website explains the app; it does not run it. There is also no Mac or Windows app. The only way to make a Danceify video is the iPhone or iPad app.

The app runs on iPad as well as iPhone, so a family iPad works. # How to Make a TikTok Dance Video From a Photo on iPhone (November 2026)

URL: https://danceifyapp.com/blog/tiktok-dance-video-from-a-photo.html
Updated: 2026-11-10

Make a TikTok dance video from one photo with Danceify, an iPhone app: pick the TikTok style (or K-Pop, Hip-hop, Reggaeton), add a track, save the 10-second video and post it to TikTok. Photo tips and what it costs.

## How to Make a TikTok Dance Video From a Photo on iPhone

Step-by-step guide · Published November 10, 2026 · Updated November 10, 2026 · 6 min read

Short answer
Danceify - AI Dance Videos, an iPhone app, turns one photo of a person, a baby, a dog or a cat into a 10-second vertical dance video. As of November 10, 2026, you pick the TikTok style (or one of 16 others), pick a track, tap CREATE, save the video and upload it in TikTok. Free to download; a Regular video uses 250 coins.

Key facts

- App: Danceify - AI Dance Videos, App Store ID 6760788471. iPhone and iPad only; no Android.
- Input: one photo. Output: a 10-second vertical video that saves to your phone.
- Styles for TikTok: TikTok Viral first; K-Pop, Hip-hop and Reggaeton also suit short vertical video. 17 styles in all.
- Music: pick a track in the app before CREATE; change it on the player; add a TikTok sound when you post.
- Cost: free download, no account. Coin packs from $3.99 (US); Creation Weekly $11.99 a week (US) with 4,000 coins. No free trial; eligible new subscribers may get the first week for $2.99 with 1,200 coins. A Regular video uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later.

A TikTok dance video normally needs someone to learn the dance and film it. Danceify skips both: you give it one photo and it makes a short clip of that person (or pet) dancing. This guide covers the whole path from photo to posted video, which photos work, where the music comes from, and what it costs. It does not cover filming yourself; for that, TikTok's own camera is the tool.

Download Danceify Free

### How do I make the video, step by step?

#### 01 Download Danceify from the App Store

Get Danceify - AI Dance Videos (App Store ID 6760788471). It is free to download. There is no account, sign-up or email; purchases go through your Apple Account.

#### 02 Tap the tab for who is in the photo

On Home, choose DOG, CAT, BABY or ADULT. The app uses this to apply the right body proportions and movement.

#### 03 Pick the TikTok style

Choose TikTok Viral from the 17 dance styles. It is the style built around the arm patterns, body rolls and direct-to-camera energy that short vertical clips use. The next section lists other styles worth trying.

#### 04 Choose one photo and a track

Pick a photo from your camera roll. One person or pet, whole body visible, good light, facing the camera. Then pick a track in the MUSIC row.

#### 05 Tap CREATE

Danceify makes a 10-second vertical dance video. A Regular video uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later (150 coins in earlier versions). You can change the track on the player once the video is ready.

#### 06 Save it and post it to TikTok

Save the video to your camera roll. Open TikTok, tap +, choose Upload, pick the video, add a sound, caption or hashtags if you want, and post. Because the video is already vertical and about 10 seconds long, nothing needs cropping or trimming.

### Which dance styles suit TikTok?

Every Danceify video is vertical and 10 seconds long, so all 17 styles can be posted. These four tend to read best on a phone screen:

- TikTok Viral: upper-body-heavy, camera-facing choreography made for this format. Start here.
- K-Pop: sharp, synchronized moves that look clean at small sizes.
- Hip-hop: loose grooves and isolations; works well on dogs and babies too.
- Reggaeton: hip-led rhythm that fits short, looping clips.

The other styles (EDM Shuffle, Salsa, Bollywood, Samba, Greek, Ballet, Tango, Flamenco, Swing, Belly Dance, Hula, Country Line, Irish) are just as valid; a ballet-dancing cat is its own kind of TikTok post. See all 17 styles.

### What photo should I use?

The photo decides most of the result. Three rules cover almost everything:

One person or pet
The app expects a single subject. Crop a group photo down to one person before you pick it.

Whole body visible
Head to feet in the frame, with a little space around. Whole-body photos dance best; the app warns you when only part of a person's body is showing. For a dog or cat, a photo showing the whole animal, sitting or standing, is enough: the app stands them up for the dance.

Good light, facing the camera
Daylight or a bright room, no backlighting, no sunglasses, no heavy filters. A front-facing or slightly angled shot gives the app a clear face to keep.

Avoid screenshots of screenshots and very small images; use the original photo from your camera roll. For more on photos, see photo to dance video.

### Where does the music come from?

Danceify includes tracks. You pick one in the MUSIC row before tapping CREATE, and you can change it on the player after the video is made. The video you save to your camera roll has that track in it.

TikTok also lets you add one of its own sounds when you upload, the same way as with any video from your camera roll. If you want a trending TikTok sound, add it in TikTok at upload time.

### Can I make a dog, cat or baby TikTok dance?

Yes. The DOG, CAT and BABY tabs on Home exist for exactly this. Use one photo of the pet or baby with the whole body visible, choose the TikTok style, and tap CREATE. The app keeps the pet's markings and the baby's face. For photo tips specific to pets, see dog dance video tips and AI cat dance; for babies, baby dance video tips. Only upload a photo of another person if they have agreed, and a photo of a child only if you are the child's parent or legal guardian.

### What does it cost?

Danceify is free to download, with no account. Videos use coins (◆): one-time coin packs start at $3.99 (US), and Creation Weekly is $11.99 a week in the US with 4,000 coins a week; eligible new subscribers may get the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins. There is no free trial. A Regular video uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later (150 coins in earlier versions), so 4,000 coins is 16 TikTok-ready videos a week. The App Store shows the price for your country. Full details: Danceify pricing explained.

### Does it work on Android?

No. Danceify is an iPhone and iPad app. The finished video is an ordinary video file, so an Android user can receive and post it, but the app itself only runs on iOS. See Is Danceify on Android?

Download Danceify on the App Store

Facts current as of November 10, 2026. Danceify is available on iOS. Creation Weekly: $11.99/week (US), no free trial; eligible new subscribers may get the first week for $2.99. Cancel anytime. TikTok is a trademark of its owner; Danceify is not affiliated with TikTok.

### Questions people ask

How do I make a TikTok dance video from a photo?

On an iPhone, download Danceify - AI Dance Videos, tap the tab for who is in the photo, choose the TikTok style, pick one clear photo and a track, and tap CREATE. Save the 10-second video to your camera roll and upload it in TikTok.

Is there a free app that makes a photo dance for TikTok?

Danceify is free to download, with no account. Making a video uses coins: one-time coin packs from $3.99 (US), or Creation Weekly at $11.99 a week (US) with 4,000 coins a week. There is no free trial; eligible new subscribers may get the first week for $2.99 with 1,200 coins.

Which Danceify dance styles look best on TikTok?

TikTok Viral is made for it. K-Pop, Hip-hop and Reggaeton also suit short vertical video. All 17 styles produce a vertical 10-second video, so any of them can be posted.

Can I use my own music or a TikTok sound?

In Danceify you pick a track in the MUSIC row before tapping CREATE and can change it on the player. When you upload the video in TikTok, you can also add a TikTok sound over it the way you would with any video.

How long is a Danceify video?

About 10 seconds, in vertical format. That fits TikTok, Instagram Reels and Stories without cropping.

Can I make my dog or cat do a TikTok dance?

Yes. Tap DOG or CAT on Home, choose the TikTok style and use one photo of the pet with its whole body visible. Babies work the same way with the BABY tab.

No. Danceify is an iPhone and iPad app. The finished video is a normal video file, so you can send it to anyone.

# How to Make an AI Dance Video in 2026 — Step-by-Step Guide

URL: https://danceifyapp.com/blog/how-to-make-ai-dance-video.html
Updated: 2026-11-10

How to turn one photo into an AI dance video with Danceify, an iPhone app: pick a person, baby, dog or cat and one of 17 dance styles. Step-by-step guide.

## How to Make an AI Dance Video in 2026

Step-by-step guide · Published September 15, 2026 · Updated November 10, 2026 · 5 min read

Short answer
Danceify - AI Dance Videos, an iPhone app, turns one photo of a person, a baby, a dog or a cat into a 10-second dance video in any of 17 dance styles. Free to download; no account.

See photo to dance video, make my dog dance, AI cat dance and dancing baby video.

Making someone dance in a video used to require actual dancing — or at least some serious video editing skills. Not anymore. AI dance video generators can now take a single photo and produce a realistic video of that person (or pet) performing choreographed dance moves. The results are surprisingly convincing, and the whole process takes a few minutes.

This guide walks you through the complete process using Danceify, an iPhone app built specifically for AI dance video generation. It supports people, babies, dogs, and cats across 17 dance styles. It is free to download, no sign-up required.

Download Danceify Free

### The 8-Step Process

#### 01 Download Danceify from the App Store

Head to the Apple App Store and search for "Danceify" or tap the link above. The app is free to download, and you do not need to create an account. Any purchases go through your Apple Account.

#### 02 Open the App — Get Your Coins

There is no email sign-up and no account; purchases go through your Apple Account. Videos use coins (◆): one-time coin packs start at $3.99 (US), and Creation Weekly is $11.99 a week in the US with 4,000 coins a week; eligible new subscribers may get the first week for $2.99 (US) with 1,200 coins. A Regular video uses 250 coins in app version 5.38 and later (150 coins in earlier versions). The App Store shows the price for your country.

#### 03 Choose Your Subject Type

On Home, tap the tab for who is in the photo: DOG, CAT, BABY or ADULT. This is not just a label — the AI uses this information to apply the correct body mechanics, proportions, and movement style. A dog doing salsa requires fundamentally different physics than a person doing salsa.

#### 04 Pick a Dance Style

This is the fun part. Choose from 17 dance styles, each with distinct choreography:

- EDM Shuffle — Fast footwork to electronic dance music
- Salsa — Latin footwork with hip movement and rhythmic flair
- Hip-Hop — Street-style grooves, pops, and isolations
- K-Pop — Sharp, synchronized Korean pop choreography
- TikTok Viral — Trending social media dance moves
- Ballet — Classical grace with arabesques and turns

Plus Bollywood, Samba, Greek Dance, Tango, Flamenco, Reggaeton, Swing, Belly Dance, Hula, Country Line, and Irish Dance. Every style works with every subject type.

#### 05 Upload a Clear Photo and Pick a Track

Select a photo from your camera roll. The AI works best with clear, well-lit images where the subject is front-facing and takes up a good portion of the frame. One subject per photo — crop out anyone else if needed. Avoid heavy filters, sunglasses, or extreme angles. Then pick a track in the MUSIC row.

#### 06 Wait for AI Generation

After you tap CREATE, the AI gets to work. The AI preserves your subject's face, features, and identity throughout the dance.

#### 07 Change the Music if You Like

Your video comes with the track you picked before tapping CREATE; you can change it on the player. The app includes a selection of tracks suited to each genre. The music syncs with the choreography to create a polished final product.

#### 08 Save and Share to Social Media

Save the finished video to your camera roll with one tap. Videos are rendered in a vertical format optimized for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and Stories. Share directly from your phone to any platform — or send it in a text message to make someone's day.

### Tips for the Best Results

Pro Tip: Lighting
Natural daylight produces the best results. If shooting indoors, face a window or use even, diffused lighting. Avoid harsh shadows across the face — the AI needs to clearly map facial features to preserve identity in the video.

Pro Tip: Photo Angle
Front-facing photos work best. Slight angles (up to about 30 degrees) are fine, but extreme side profiles or overhead shots can confuse the AI. The closer to a straight-on shot, the better the dance output will look.

Pro Tip: Subject Framing
The subject should fill a good portion of the frame, with the whole body in view: whole-body photos dance best, and the app warns you when only part of a person's body is showing. Leave a bit of space around the subject rather than cropping too tight.

Pro Tip: Pet Photos
For dogs and cats, use a photo where the pet is looking toward the camera. Clear shots of their face and body give the AI enough detail to preserve breed-specific features like fur markings, ear shape, and coloring. The AI will render them standing on their hind legs with choreography designed for their body type.

### Common Mistakes to Avoid

- Group photos — The AI expects one subject per image. Crop to a single person or pet.
- Sunglasses or masks — Anything that covers the face makes identity preservation harder.
- Very low resolution — Avoid screenshots of screenshots or heavily compressed images. Use the original photo from your camera roll.
- Dark or backlit photos — If you can barely see the subject's face, the AI will struggle too.
- Heavy filters — Beauty filters and heavy edits can distort facial geometry. Use the original, unfiltered photo.

# Baby Dance Video Tips: Best Photos and Styles for an AI Dancing Baby Video
